title: LucidPath API credits-to-pilot & hosting pathway discussion
summary: Intro discovery call for LucidPath (startup building contextual search for enterprise docs). Discussed PLG/self-serve onramp, free credits to run an initial pilot, rough time-to-first-token (TTFT) goals, and decision criteria between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Customer emphasized security (SOC 2, SSO/SAML), data residency, and predictable cost per 1k tokens. SE walked through quickstart steps, demo checklist, and benchmark approach. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot using hosted API credits and a follow-up deep dive if latency/quality needs dedicated/private options.
next_steps: Samira to send tailored pilot credit grant + onboarding doc (by 2026-07-02)
Jordan to share simple benchmark script and dataset checklist (by 2026-07-03)
LucidPath to confirm internal pilot participants and provide sample doc set (by 2026-07-06)
Schedule technical deep dive (private/dedicated fit) if pilot shows latency issues (tentative week of 2026-07-13)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (CTO, LucidPath), Ethan Cole (Eng Mgr), Priya Sharma (Product)

Summary/Topics (auto): free credits, TTFT, hosted/dedicated/private, security, benchmarks, next steps

00:00 Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Samira from Redwood, i'm the account exec, appreciate you making time, quick roll call?
00:06 Maya: maya here, CTO at LucidPath. hey Samira.
00:08 Ethan: Ethan, engineering manager.
00:10 Priya: Priya, product.
00:12 Jordan: Jordan from Redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll walk through the quickstart and perf checks.
00:20 Samira: perfect, goal today is to figure out how fast we can get you to first token, what pilot looks like, and whether hosted is good enough or we need dedicated/private setups.
00:34 Maya: yeah our biggest constraints are security and predictable cost. we process internal legal and product docs, a lot of PII-ish content, and we need SOC 2 controls, SSO, and an audit trail. but we also want to move fast.
00:48 Jordan: completely get that. so typical path for teams like you is PLG/self-serve with a small hosted credit pilot. you can try the API with the SDK or curl, get to first token in under an hour for basic calls, then run a 1-2 week evaluation under credits to measure latency/cost.
01:05 Priya: under an hour? that's optimistic — what does that include? spinning up keys, first request, auth?
01:12 Jordan: yes, create an account, we send credits, you'll have an API key. SDK has examples for node and python, there's also a quick curl example. if you want streaming or tool-calls that's a bit more setup but still same day. most teams hit first token in 20-60 minutes if they follow quickstart.
01:30 Ethan: ok, what about hosting choices — when do we bump into dedicated or private?
01:36 Jordan: great question. Hosted is easiest: you get our managed catalog and latency/cost tradeoffs are transparent. Dedicated if you need reserved GPU capacity — predictable throughput and SLAs. Private (VPC or on-prem) if you need customer-controlled network and strict compliance.
01:52 Maya: for us SOC 2 and SSO are table stakes. do you support SAML/SSO and audit logs on hosted?
01:58 Samira: yes, hosted supports SSO via SAML/Okta integrations and we surface audit logs; for certain enterprise contracts we also provide extended retention and enhanced logging. Jordan can share the security doc.
02:12 Jordan: i'll drop the SOC 2 and security whitepaper after the call — it covers KMS integrations, encryption at rest/in transit, RBAC and audit log samples. note: for absolute data residency or air-gapped requirements we recommend Private.
02:30 Maya: got it. and how do we think about cost — we need predictable per-1k token cost, and some ops will be very latency-sensitive.
02:39 Jordan: our pricing model for hosted is usage-based; for Dedicated you can purchase reserved capacity which yields predictable unit economics. for latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend setting routing policy to low-latency models and enabling prefix caching / KV cache features.
02:55 Ethan: can you explain KV cash? i mean KV cache — i've seen that in docs but not sure how it impacts throughput.
03:01 Jordan: yep KV cache, sorry the transcript might show "KV cash" sometimes — it's basically a way to store and re-use previous KV entries (model key-value cache) to reduce repeated attention costs; helps latency and token cost for conversational workloads.
03:20 Priya: interesting. for pilot scope we want to test document-to-answer latency and cost on a 50k-doc sample, is that realistic in a 2-week pilot?
03:30 Jordan: yes, 2 weeks is fine. we'd suggest a tiered benchmark: small sample (100 docs) to confirm TTFT and integration, then medium (5k) to check median latency, and heavier (50k) to test throughput and caching gains. we'll provide a simple benchmark script.
03:48 Samira: linking to credits — we can provision $2k in hosted credits to run the 2-week pilot and we can extend if there's clear progress.
03:58 Maya: that's helpful. are there hard limits with hosted credits? like concurrency or rate limits?
04:05 Jordan: hosted accounts have default rate limits but for pilot we can temporarily raise them. if you need guaranteed concurrency and throughput that's when Dedicated becomes attractive because you get reserved capacity and autoscaling controls.
04:20 Ethan: ok, about measurement — what exact metrics should we capture to evaluate whether hosted is sufficient?
04:27 Jordan: key metrics: median and p95 latency for your sample prompts, tokens per second throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and success rate / error rate. also track how much benefit you get from prefix/KV caching — measure same workload with caching on/off.
04:45 Maya: i'm also worried about prompt leakage or accidental retention — how does hosted handle data retention?
04:52 Samira: we offer data retention controls; by default transient logs exist for debugging but can be turned off for accounts; for regulated customers we recommend Private or Dedicated with stricter retention policies. we'll summarize retention options in the security doc.
05:10 Priya: how long to spin up a Private environment if we chose that later?
05:15 Jordan: Private timelines vary: VPC-based private deploy typically 4-6 weeks for initial setup and network runbook, on-prem longer depending on ops. Dedicated can be provisioned faster — often within a week if capacity available. For PLG pilot you almost always start hosted.
05:34 Ethan: any SDK or infra work to be mindful of? like cache hooks, or modifying inference calls for streaming?
05:40 Jordan: SDKs are pretty straightforward; for streaming the SDK has event listeners. you should also instrument token-level logging for cost breakdowns and include tracing headers for request-level debugging. samira: we have a small integration guide with screenshots.
05:58 Maya: we have an internal compliance review early next month; can you provide a SOC 2 cert and a contact for security questions?
06:04 Samira: yes, SOC 2 report and security contact. jordan i'll make introduction.
06:10 Jordan: happy to be the security contact. i'll include our compliance package and a short FAQ for your review.
06:20 Priya: wanted to ask about model variants — do you have smaller quantized models to save cost and reduce latency?
06:27 Jordan: we do, and we also provide quantization recommendations per workload. for higher throughput you can pick a lower-cost variant and configure routing policy to fall back to higher quality when needed. Redwood Optimize also suggests batching/caching configs.
06:45 Ethan: can we run a cheap baseline locally to sanity check before hitting hosted? some teams do a tiny local LLM for smoke tests.
06:51 Jordan: totally — that's common. run a local 7B quantized model for integration tests, then run real evals on Redwood to measure production behavior.
06:59 Maya: i'd like the TTFT number in writing — what should i tell execs?
07:04 Samira: for basic integration (API key, simple call, SDK) TTFT < 1 hour; practical first test call and small eval results within 1-2 days; meaningful pilot metrics across your 50k sample in 2 weeks. we'll put those expectations in the pilot doc.
07:20 Priya: ok, what's the rollback story if a higher-latency model suddenly regresses?
07:26 Jordan: we have rollouts and automatic fallback policies; you can do canary deploys, A/B test models, and set automatic fallback to a compatible variant on errors or performance regressions.
07:36 Maya: any notes on data residency — we operate in EU and US, need a region that keeps data inside EU for certain customers.
07:44 Jordan: we offer region controls for hosted and full isolation in Private; for EU-only data residency we can pin requests to the EU region; for stronger guarantees Private is recommended.
07:58 Ethan: ok this is helpful. should we run a smoke test tomorrow?
08:03 Samira: sure — we can provision credits today and Jordan will send the quickstart. Samira: i'll email the onboarding steps and make the credit grant.
08:12 Jordan: i'll attach the benchmark script (python + curl), the perf checklist, and the security docs in one package.
08:18 Priya: great. last question — any gotchas with token counting or billing that trips teams up?
08:24 Jordan: watch for system prompts and hidden tokens in some chat formats; also streaming vs non-streaming can change token accounting. instrument token logs early.
08:36 Maya: ok thanks everyone. let's recap next steps.
08:40 Samira: recap: Samira grant $2k credits + onboarding doc; Jordan share benchmark script and security pack; LucidPath provide sample corpus and security contacts; follow-up technical deep dive after initial pilot measurement.
08:55 Ethan: will do. thanks.
09:00 End of recording.
